title: Check complementary slackness numerically

blocks.text: A bakery's planning tool solves its daily LP with one solver and stores the plan and the row prices. The owner wants an independent check, run on every saved result, that the pair really is optimal: a list of every place where it breaks complementary slackness, empty when the pair is fine.

The bakery's LP, with $`A`$ the products, $`R`$ the rows, $`v_j`$ the profit per tray of product $`j`$, $`a_{ij}`$ its coefficient in row $`i`$ (0 if absent) and $`b_i`$ the right-hand side; each row is a limit ($`\le`$) or a minimum ($`\ge`$):
\max \sum_{j \in A} v_j\, x_j \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{j \in A} a_{ij}\, x_j \;(\le \text{ or } \ge)\; b_i \;\; \forall i \in R, \qquad x_j \ge 0

items: the **slack** of a $`\le`$ row is $`b_i - \sum_j a_{ij} x_j`$, and of a $`\ge`$ row $`\sum_j a_{ij} x_j - b_i`$;
the **reduced cost** of product $`j`$ is $`d_j = v_j - \sum_{i \in R} a_{ij}\, y_i`$;
complementary slackness asks $`\text{slack}_i \cdot y_i = 0`$ for every row and $`x_j \cdot d_j = 0`$ for every product.

blocks.text: Write `cs_violations(value, rows, plan, prices, tol=1e-6)` in `cs.py`. `value` maps each product to $`v_j`$; `rows` maps each row's name to `(coefficients, sense, rhs)`, `sense` being `"<="` or `">="`; `plan` maps each product to $`x_j`$; `prices` maps each row to $`y_i`$. Return the sorted list of the names of every row with slack and price both nonzero, and every product with value and reduced cost both nonzero, where "nonzero" means larger than `tol` in absolute value (the stored numbers come from a floating-point solver). The plans the tests pass satisfy every row.

cases.says: the optimal plan with its prices has no violation, and plans that leave a priced row slack or use an activity with a nonzero reduced cost are flagged
slack, prices, values and reduced costs within the tolerance count as zero
a >= row's slack is how far the plan is above the minimum
a reduced cost subtracts the prices of every row the activity is in, >= rows included

origin.section: Complementary Slackness: Slack Rows Have Price Zero, Used Variables Have Reduced Cost Zero

concepts: at the optimum a row with slack has price zero and a variable in use has reduced cost zero
